AdaSteer: Adaptive Shared Timestep Embedding Efficient Residual

Methodology

AdaSteer operates on the timestep embedding pathway. In LongCat-Video, the timestep embedder produces \(t \in \mathbb{R}^{512}\), which each block's adaLN projects into shift, scale, and gate vectors:

$$t \;\xrightarrow{\;\text{adaLN}_i\;}\; \bigl[\gamma_i^{\text{msa}},\, \beta_i^{\text{msa}},\, \alpha_i^{\text{msa}},\, \gamma_i^{\text{mlp}},\, \beta_i^{\text{mlp}},\, \alpha_i^{\text{mlp}}\bigr] \in \mathbb{R}^{6 \times 4096}$$

AdaSteer learns a single additive offset \(\delta \in \mathbb{R}^{512}\) applied before this projection:

$$t' = t + \delta$$

Because each block has its own frozen adaLN projection (SiLU + Linear: 512→24,576), the same \(\delta\) produces block-specific perturbations to modulation vectors. This is a structured weight-tying strategy: all 48 blocks share 512 trainable inputs, but the pretrained projections act as learned de-tying transforms, providing per-block specialization for free.

We also explore a TinyLoRA variant operating on attention weights via truncated SVD:

$$y = Wx + \tfrac{\alpha}{r}\, U_r\!\bigl(v \odot (V_r^\top x)\bigr)$$

With \(r\!=\!2\), 48 blocks, and 2 target modules per block, TinyLoRA trains 192 scalars. Full weight tying reduces this to 4. Both methods use 10 steps of Adam (lr=0.005) on the flow-matching denoising loss over the 14 conditioning frames. No future-frame supervision. Adapted parameters are discarded after generation.

Introduction

Video diffusion transformers achieve state-of-the-art generation quality, but their inference is instance-agnostic: the same frozen weights process every test video regardless of its content, motion, and style. Test-time adaptation (TTA) offers a remedy—briefly adapting a pretrained model on a single test instance before generation—but applying TTA to large-scale video DiTs (10B+ parameters) presents a fundamental challenge: the extreme asymmetry between model capacity and the available adaptation signal (typically 14 frames, ~300K latent values).

We introduce AdaSteer (Adaptive Shared Timestep Embedding Efficient Residual), a TTA method that steers a frozen video DiT by learning a single additive perturbation \(\delta \in \mathbb{R}^{512}\) to the timestep embedding shared across all 48 transformer blocks. Each block's frozen adaLN projection then maps this shared perturbation into block-specific modulation of the 4096-dim hidden states (shift, scale, and gate for self-attention and MLP). This is a structured weight-tying strategy: all blocks share one 512-dim trainable input, but the pretrained adaLN projections act as learned de-tying transforms, producing 48 distinct high-dimensional modulations from one compact perturbation.

We evaluate on LongCat-Video (13.6B-parameter DiT, 48 blocks, hidden dim 4096) in the video continuation setting: given 14 observed frames at 480p, the model generates 28 future frames. We compare against LoRA (ranks 1–8, 5–20 steps), full-model fine-tuning (13.6B params), and a no-TTA baseline on Panda-70M and UCF-101.

Experimental Results

On Panda-70M (100 videos, 480p), AdaSteer achieves FVD = 561.1, a reduction of 80 points (12.5%%) over the no-TTA baseline (641.1), at +54s compute per video (67%% overhead). Per-frame metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS) remain unchanged, indicating AdaSteer improves distributional quality—temporal coherence and motion realism—rather than per-pixel fidelity.

LoRA-based TTA fails to improve FVD across all tested configs. Sweeping rank \(\in\{1,4,8\}\), block subsets, step counts (5–20), and LRs (\(10^{-5}\) to \(2\!\times\!10^{-4}\)), the best LoRA achieves FVD = 644.6 (baseline: 641.1). Higher LRs cause catastrophic overfitting (PSNR drops from 18.6 to 17.4). Full-model TTA shows +0.01 PSNR.

An 8-way ablation isolates auxiliary features: early stopping gains marginal FVD (−85 vs −80) but doubles training time; augmentation improves PSNR (+0.05 dB) but hurts FVD by 26 points; CLIP gating and gradient accumulation provide no benefit. Bare AdaSteer is the Pareto-optimal configuration.

Next Steps

(1) 1000-video full-scale Panda-70M evaluation (running); (2) TinyLoRA ablation: 13 configs exploring SVD rank, weight tying, target scope, block subsets (running); (3) SAVi-DNO comparison adapted for DiT backbone; (4) investigating the distributional-vs-pointwise quality tradeoff under rank-1 constraints.
